record_type_quote: The two main goals of this study were: (a) the validation of the German version of the GSQ according to the Universalist model of cross-cultural adaptation [ 29 ] and (b) the replication of sensory processing differences of individuals with higher or lower AQ scores as reported in the original English version by Robertson and Simmons [ 48 ] and in the French version of Sapey-Triomphe et al. [ 51 ].

targets.title: The relationship between sensory sensitivity and autistic traits in the general population
targets.evidence_quote: The two main goals of this study were: (a) the validation of the German version of the GSQ according to the Universalist model of cross-cultural adaptation [ 29 ] and (b) the replication of sensory processing differences of individuals with higher or lower AQ scores as reported in the original English version by Robertson and Simmons [ 48 ] and in the French version of Sapey-Triomphe et al. [ 51 ].
targets.outcome_quote: Contrary to expectations, only 35 out of 297 students had AQ scores higher than 26 in our sample. Therefore, the present sample seems not suitable for drawing meaningful conclusions about the sensory processing differences of individuals with higher AQ scores.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors also call the replication unsuccessful, but explicitly judge their sample unsuitable for meaningful conclusions because too few participants had high AQ. The codebook special verdict for a non-adjudicating attempt takes precedence. Both named targets are included in the replication objective.

Other validation studies supply background or comparison data, rather than an additional specific finding targeted here. The explicit sample-defect judgment determines the special outcome for both targets.
